title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68) comparing ungated LLM generation (baseline) to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline. Generation used gpt-5-mini with a shared-initial-generation protocol (one candidate per intent shared by both arms). The guarded arm validated the shared candidate with a deterministic validator and applied at most one deterministic repair iteration when eligible. Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline emulator-executable successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.0); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact binomial) on discordant counts yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 15 percentage-point target effect is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We summarize the deterministic validator checks, the repair operator’s deterministic heuristics and invocation rule, the exact small-discordant-count inferential implementation, representative difficulty metadata available in the task manifest, and operational limitations (shared-generation estimand, synthetic tasks, single LLM, bounded repair budget, emulator fidelity). All prompts, traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution and analysis bundles described in the evidence manifest.

sections.introduction: Automating NetOps with generative LLMs promises efficiency but risks producing syntactically plausible yet operationally unsafe or incomplete configurations (incorrect ordering, missing prerequisites, protected-interface violations). Prior work proposes verifier-assisted architectures and iterative repair, but end-to-end, execution-grounded evidence quantifying the marginal efficacy of bounded deterministic repair on identical LLM candidates is limited. We preregistered a narrowly scoped paired experiment to answer the research question: Does an iterative generate–verify–repair pipeline that pairs hosted-LLM generation with deterministic verification and bounded deterministic repair (≤1 iteration) yield a higher emulator-executable configuration success rate than ungated LLM generation when both arms receive the same initial LLM candidate? Our principal contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) under a shared-initial-generation estimand; (2) exact paired counts and the small-discordant-count inferential implementation; and (3) a concise, reproducible description of the deterministic validator and repair operator used in the guarded pipeline together with operational interpretation.
sections.related_work: Surveys and prototypes document active use of LLMs for intent-to-configuration translation and co-pilot assistance while reporting hallucinations and schema violations as recurring failure modes. Mitigations across domains include retrieval-augmented generation, constrained decoding, live schema grounding and verifier-assisted repair loops; these reduce but do not eliminate structured-output errors. Formal verification formalisms (NetKAT variants, ensemble verifiers) can detect reachability and isolation violations but face fidelity and scalability trade-offs when modelling control-plane dynamics. Position and architecture papers on agentic NetOps emphasize that operational reliability depends on surrounding assurance machinery (evidence traces, bounded tool use, rollback policies) as much as base LLM capability. Our study complements that literature by isolating whether a deterministic repair operator can correct the same LLM candidate identified as invalid by a deterministic validator (the shared-candidate estimand), a narrower question than studies allowing independent resampling or LLM-invoked repairs.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design: The experimental plan, frozen before execution, defined a paired shared-initial-generation design with n=200 confirmatory natural-language NetOps intents spanning single-device and small multi-device changes (ACLs, VLAN/MTU updates, uplink switchover patterns). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Model and budget: declared model gpt-5-mini; maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized hosted-model calls used = 201. Execution environment: Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) performed canonical parsing, structural/workflow checks and a deterministic final-state simulation. Outcome definition: success = validator reports validation_after.valid == true after applying the candidate to the emulator. Missingness and retries: transient provider/API errors allowed a single automatic retry per preregistered policy; provider/API failures counted as failures for the primary analysis.

Deterministic validator (concise description): the validator pipeline applied three ordered checks. First, syntactic parse and canonical normalization convert CLI-like lines into a normalized_configuration and tokenized commands; parse failures are invalid. Second, structural and workflow checks verify presence of required commands, dependency/order constraints (make-before-break, shutdown/configure/restore patterns), group-activity constraints (exactly-one / minimum-active in groups) and protected-interface rules. Third, the validator deterministically simulates applying the normalized configuration to the emulator model and compares observed final_state fields against the task’s expected_final_state. Violations are categorized (e.g., SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR, MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION, FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH, TRANSIENT_RULE_VIOLATION) and exposed in the validator trace for repair or human escalation.

Deterministic repair operator (algorithmic, rule-based): the guarded pipeline invoked a deterministic repair operator (no LLM calls) only when the validator returned violation_count>0 and the violation types were within the operator’s repairable family. The operator implements deterministic, auditable transformations to the normalized_configuration via three canonical steps: (1) insertion: add missing required commands explicitly identified by the validator (for example, inserting a required shutdown/restore command pair), (2) reordering: move command blocks to satisfy dependency or make-before-break constraints (atomic block reordering preserving command groups), and (3) preservation: enforce task-level preserve_unspecified_state and protected-interface constraints by rejecting or rewriting candidate lines that would modify protected fields. Each transformation is deterministic and annotated in a repair trace. Repair invocation rule: at most one deterministic repair per episode (bounded repair budget ≤1); repair applied only to MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND or DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION families where the mapping from violation to insertion/reordering is deterministic and unambiguous. All validator inputs/outputs and repair traces are archived in the execution bundle.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and raw outcomes: the run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 pairs) with zero provider/API failures; hosted-model calls used = 201 (shared_initial_generation=200, repair=1). Artifact-backed primary counts: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). The paired contingency is n11=199, n10=1 (guarded-only), n01=0 (baseline-only), n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Repair and failure accounting: initial validator failures (validation_before.valid == false) occurred in exactly one episode of the confirmatory set. Deterministic repair invocations = 1; that single repair converted the validator-failing candidate into a validator-passing configuration yielding the sole guarded-only success. Syntactic parse failures = 0. No confirmatory episodes were unscorable or excluded under the preregistered contamination rules; the complete-pair count = 200.

Statistical inference (exact implementation and justification): the preregistered primary test is McNemar’s test for paired binary outcomes implemented in its exact (binomial) form suitable for small discordant counts. Under the exact McNemar (binomial) formulation the number of discordant pairs in one direction follows Binomial(n = n10 + n01, p = 0.5) under the null of equal marginal probabilities; the two-sided p-value is the two-sided binomial tail probability for the observed ordering. With observed discordant counts n10 = 1 and n01 = 0, n = 1 and the exact two-sided binomial p-value equals 1.0 (no evidence to reject equality). Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap seed 1729) yielding [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered detectable effect (15 percentage points) assumed a baseline ≈0.50; the observed near-ceiling baseline (0.995) materially reduces power to detect large absolute gains and explains why the preregistered alternative is excluded by the observed CI.

Representative difficulty metadata: representative tasks (6 archived exemplars) show difficulty levels {medium:1, hard:2, very_hard:3, easy:0} illustrating that the confirmatory set includes nontrivial patterns (make-before-break, paired MTU changes, constrained group policies). The full per-task difficulty distribution for all 200 confirmatory intents is recorded in the archived execution/task_manifest.jsonl and is available in the evidence bundle; per-task metadata were used during curation but the confirmatory inference above reports the artifact-backed paired counts.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation relative to the estimand: the shared-initial-generation estimand isolates whether a deterministic repair operator can correct the same LLM candidate judged invalid by a deterministic validator. Under this estimand and the curated confirmatory distribution, ungated gpt-5-mini generation already produced near-perfect candidates (199/200), so bounded deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yielded a marginal operational improvement (one additional pass). This narrow result does not assess architectures that permit independent re-sampling (per-arm fresh LLM calls), multi-step LLM-invoked repairs, or human-in-the-loop escalation policies; those broader operational designs can increase practical gains at the expense of more model calls and more complex governance.

Operational implications: deterministic validator gates serve important assurance roles even when baseline generation is high-quality: they (a) prevent execution of invalid candidates, (b) emit structured violation codes that permit prioritized human review or automated rule-based repair, and (c) produce auditable traces for post-hoc investigation. When baseline LLM performance is near-ceiling, bounded deterministic repairs applied to the same candidate offer limited marginal benefit; however, in harder or adversarial distributions (or with independent-resampling estimands) verifier-assisted strategies permitting additional LLM calls or staged repair budgets are likely to provide larger improvements.

Threats to validity (brief, artifact-grounded): internal validity — single model and single prompt template may induce prompt sensitivity; design choice of shared-initial-generation intentionally isolates repair-on-same-candidate but reduces evaluation of independent-resampling architectures; repair budget bounded to one iteration limits observed repair yield. Construct validity — emulator and validator are deterministic and may not capture asynchronous control-plane behaviors (e.g., BGP convergence timing) or vendor-specific CLI idiosyncrasies; final-state simulation compares emulator-state to expected_final_state but cannot replicate all production dynamics. External validity — single LLM (gpt-5-mini), synthetic curated tasks, and a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator limit generalization to production NetOps with multivendor devices, real traffic conditions, and adversarial operators. Conclusion validity — near-ceiling baseline compresses discordant counts, reducing observable effect sizes for the preregistered 15 pp target; the exact McNemar binomial implementation and bootstrap CI were selected and executed as preregistered to correctly treat small-discordant regimes.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to evaluate whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves the emulator-executable success rate of LLM-generated NetOps configurations when both arms receive the same initial candidate. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the GVR pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The artifact-backed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) and therefore does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target due to the realized near-ceiling baseline. For the studied estimand and distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate produced negligible marginal gain; practitioners should treat deterministic validators as essential assurance gates and consider estimand and repair-budget trade-offs (shared-candidate vs independent-resampling, bounded rule-based repair vs LLM-invoked repair) when designing operational NetOps pipelines. Future work should evaluate independent-resampling guarded designs, multi-vendor CLI diversity, adversarial or out-of-distribution intents, larger repair budgets, and higher-fidelity control-plane emulation to better characterize when GVR guards yield substantive operational benefits.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, study selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting. Models and tooling: generation used gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records requested_model 'gpt-5-mini'); validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scorer_id/scorer_version and scoring_rule 'full_intent_constraint_validation' are recorded in scoring artifacts); execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Key preregistered settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; analysis plan = exact McNemar two-sided with paired bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes (200 pairs) using 201 hosted-model calls; provider-call stage_counts record shared_initial_generation=200 and repair=1. All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair), analysis artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the manuscript (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).
limitations: Synthetic, curated task set focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLIs, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.

Emulator (Dockerized Mininet+FRR) and deterministic validator model control-plane behavior but do not fully capture production runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration in the confirmatory protocol; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.

Shared-initial-generation design (single initial candidate per intent shared across arms) reduced model-call cost and isolated repair effectiveness on identical candidates but reduces external generalizability compared with independent re-sampling per arm.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Aggregate task-difficulty metadata (easy / medium / hard / very_hard) for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) and may be inspected in the evidence bundle for per-task difficulty counts; the per-task manifest underlies task curation but full distributional counts are presented in the archived manifest rather than inline here.
